subject: Tool-calling integration patterns - postcall recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@finapps.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T17:12:00Z
Subject: Tool-calling integration patterns - postcall recap & next steps

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps focused on the integration/architecture items you asked about. TL;DR: Redwood can support SDK-based auth, multiple routing policies, structured output/tool-calling, and embeddings/reranking — below are recommended patterns and the short action plan.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary use case: enrich FinApps product help & workflows with LLM tool-calling (data fetch, transaction status, reranker over CRM embeddings).
- Priority integrations: account lookups (internal API), transactions tool (idempotent actions), and a reranker over embeddings for search results.
- Non-negotiables: audit logs, customer-managed KMS for keys, and network isolation for production.

Recommended integration patterns (summary)
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Use Redwood SDK (server-side) with short-lived tokens bound to service identity. For VPC/private installs we recommend mTLS between your runtime and the Redwood private endpoint + KMS-backed key wrapping.
   - For user-scoped actions, issue per-session tokens tied to user id and scopes.

2) Routing & model variants
   - Route by policy: dev -> smaller open model; prod -> quantized, high-throughput variant. Fallback policy to second-best model on load.

3) Structured output & tool/function calling
   - Define explicit tool schemas: name, input schema (JSON Schema), auth requirements, idempotency, timeout.
   - Use Redwood's function-calling layer to map model responses to tool invocations; prefer explicit tool definitions over free-form instruction to avoid hallucinations.
   - For parallel tools: run non-conflicting calls concurrently (e.g., account details + recent activity), then merge outputs; serialize state-changing tools (transactions) behind an orchestrator to preserve idempotency.
   - Error handling: canonical retry policy (2 fast retries), circuit-breaker for downstream failures, and a fallback prompt flow that surfaces partial results to user with action suggestions.

4) Embeddings & reranker pattern
   - Index your canonical content with sentence-level embeddings. Use a two-stage pipeline: candidate retrieval (approx nearest neighbors) + model-based reranker that uses context + tool outputs. Cache reranker decisions for repeated queries.

Action items / next steps
- I attach a short architecture diagram and a SDK quickstart for your engs to try.
- Proposed technical deep dive: 60 min with your backend & security teams next week to go over auth/KMS and orchestration patterns.
- Please share the name for your SRE contact to set up a test VPC connection (if you want to evaluate Private).

Attachments: Proposal-architecture-diagram.pdf (architecture diagram), redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (code + README)

Thanks — happy to align on dates.

—

Sarah — great questions. Answers inline below then a proposed MAP (mutual action plan) and a link to a short technical note.

1) Token validation
- Redwood issues signed JWTs you can validate locally via JWKS for many flows. For customer-managed Private installs we additionally support KMS-wrapped short-lived certs and mTLS for service-to-service. We can provide a sample JWKS endpoint and verification snippet in the SDK.

2) Idempotency & orchestration
- Idempotency pattern: require a client-provided idempotency_key for any state-changing tool. The Redwood orchestrator stores the key and outcome (success/failure) for a configurable TTL (we suggest 24-72h).
- Exactly-once: if you need strict semantics, place the authoritative write in your service and call Redwood only for LLM reasoning/validation+tool suggestion. For many workflows Redwood can act as the decision engine and call your idempotent endpoint with idempotency_key enforced.

Parallel tools & error handling
- Parallelism: safe for read-only tools (account read, recent transactions); for any write/action tools we recommend serial execution or external orchestration to avoid race conditions.
- Retries & fallbacks: Redwood supports a retry policy (2 retries, exponential backoff) and a circuit-breaker that trips on repeated downstream 5xx/errors. We recommend surface partial results and a human confirmation step for ambiguous failures.

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan)
- This week: FinApps engs try the attached quickstart and confirm they can validate JWTs locally. (Owner: FinApps)
- Next week: 60-min technical deep dive (Owner: Redwood). Proposed windows: Tue/Wed 10-12 PST.
- Week after: limited PoC with 1-2 tool definitions (account fetch + reranker). (Owner: joint).

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.com/deal/rd-2026-4832), tech note (https://docs.redwood.ai/tool-calling-overview)
